title: The Mughal Empire
subtitle: From Babur at Panipat to the last emperor in Rangoon · 1526 – 1857
subject: mughal-empire
intro: Founded by Babur, a Timurid prince from Central Asia, the Mughal Empire ruled most of the subcontinent at its height and shaped its administration, art and architecture. After Aurangzeb's long Deccan war it broke up into successor states — among them the Marathas, Hyderabad and Bengal — and the emperors in Delhi became pensioners first of the Marathas and then of the British, until the revolt of 1857 ended the dynasty.

events.title: First Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan ruling from Kabul, defeats Ibrahim Lodi, Sultan of Delhi, using field guns and mobile cavalry. The Lodi Sultanate falls and the Mughal dynasty begins.

events.title: Battle of Khanwa
events.summary: Babur defeats a Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga of Mewar, securing his hold on north India.

events.title: Babur dies; Humayun succeeds
events.summary: Babur dies at Agra after only four years in India, leaving his memoir, the Baburnama, and an unconsolidated kingdom to his son Humayun.

events.title: Battle of Chausa
events.summary: The Afghan leader Sher Shah Suri surprises and defeats Humayun's army on the Ganga.

events.title: Sher Shah's reforms
events.summary: In five years Sher Shah Suri reorganises revenue collection, introduces the silver rupiya and rebuilds the great road from Bengal to the Punjab. Much of this is later adopted by the Mughals.

events.title: Battle of Kannauj — Humayun loses his empire
events.summary: Sher Shah defeats Humayun again near Kannauj. Humayun flees to Persia, and for fifteen years north India is ruled by the Sur dynasty.

events.title: Humayun regains Delhi
events.summary: With Persian help, Humayun returns from exile and retakes Delhi and Agra from the quarrelling Sur successors.

events.title: Humayun dies
events.summary: Humayun dies after falling down the stairs of his library in Delhi. His 13-year-old son Akbar is enthroned, with Bairam Khan as regent. Humayun's Tomb, built later, becomes a model for Mughal architecture.

events.title: Second Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Hemu, the Hindu general who had seized Delhi in the name of the Sur dynasty, is winning until an arrow strikes his eye. His army breaks; Akbar's rule is secured.

events.title: Akbar takes power himself
events.summary: Akbar dismisses his regent Bairam Khan and begins to rule in his own right.

events.title: Rajput alliances; jizya abolished
events.summary: Akbar marries a princess of Amber and brings Rajput rulers into imperial service as commanders. In 1564 he abolishes the jizya tax on non-Muslims — the foundation of a broad-based empire.

events.title: Fall of Chittorgarh
events.summary: After a four-month siege Akbar storms Chittor, the fortress of Mewar, and massacres much of its population. Mewar itself does not submit.

events.title: Fatehpur Sikri built
events.summary: Akbar builds a new red-sandstone capital at Fatehpur Sikri near Agra, his court there until about 1585.

events.title: Conquest of Gujarat
events.summary: Gujarat, with its ports and trade, is annexed. Surat becomes the empire's main port — later raided by Shivaji.

events.title: Battle of Haldighati
events.summary: A Mughal army led by Man Singh of Amber fights Maharana Pratap of Mewar. Pratap is forced from the field but continues to resist from the hills for the rest of his life, becoming a lasting symbol of Rajput independence.

events.title: Subahs, mansabdars and Todar Mal's revenue system
events.summary: The empire is divided into provinces (subahs), officials are ranked in the mansabdari system, and Todar Mal's survey-based land revenue system is introduced — structures that outlast the dynasty.

events.title: Sulh-i-kul and the Din-i Ilahi
events.summary: After years of debates among scholars of many faiths, Akbar promotes 'sulh-i-kul' (peace with all) and a small devotional circle around himself, the Din-i Ilahi. Abul Fazl records the reign in the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.

events.title: Into the Deccan: Ahmadnagar
events.summary: Chand Bibi defends Ahmadnagar against the Mughals in 1595; the city falls in 1600. The rest of the sultanate fights on under Malik Ambar for another generation.

events.title: Akbar dies; Jahangir succeeds
events.summary: Akbar dies at Agra after a 49-year reign. His son Salim takes the throne as Jahangir.

events.title: Execution of Guru Arjan
events.summary: The fifth Sikh Guru, compiler of the Adi Granth, is executed at Lahore on Jahangir's orders after being accused of supporting a rebel prince — a turning point in Sikh–Mughal relations.

events.title: Jahangir marries Nur Jahan
events.summary: Nur Jahan becomes the most powerful woman in Mughal history, issuing coins and orders in her own name during Jahangir's later years.

events.title: English ambassador at court
events.summary: Sir Thomas Roe, sent by James I, spends four years at Jahangir's court seeking trading rights for the English East India Company.

events.title: Shah Jahan crowned
events.summary: After a rebellion against his father and the elimination of rivals, Prince Khurram is crowned Shah Jahan at Agra.

events.title: The Taj Mahal
events.summary: After Mumtaz Mahal dies in childbirth in 1631, Shah Jahan builds her tomb at Agra — the Taj Mahal, the high point of Mughal architecture.

events.title: Ahmadnagar extinguished; Deccan treaties
events.summary: The Mughals and Bijapur partition the last of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate; Bijapur and Golconda accept Mughal overlordship. Shahaji Bhosale, Shivaji's father, moves into Bijapur's service.

events.title: Shahjahanabad and the Red Fort
events.summary: Shah Jahan builds a new walled capital at Delhi, Shahjahanabad, with the Red Fort as its palace. The court moves there in 1648.

events.title: Kandahar lost to Persia
events.summary: The Safavids take Kandahar and three costly Mughal sieges fail to retake it.

events.title: War of succession
events.summary: When Shah Jahan falls ill his four sons fight for the throne. Aurangzeb defeats Dara Shikoh at Samugarh (1658), confines Shah Jahan in Agra Fort, crowns himself, and has Dara — a mystic scholar who translated the Upanishads into Persian — executed in 1659.

events.title: Shivaji's challenge
events.summary: Shivaji builds an independent Maratha kingdom in the Deccan, sacks Surat (1664), escapes from Agra (1666) and is crowned in 1674.

events.title: Battle of Saraighat
events.summary: The Ahom general Lachit Borphukan defeats a Mughal fleet and army on the Brahmaputra near Guwahati, checking Mughal expansion into Assam.

events.title: Execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur
events.summary: The ninth Sikh Guru is executed in Delhi on Aurangzeb's orders. His son, Guru Gobind Singh, later founds the Khalsa (1699).

events.title: Jizya reimposed
events.summary: Aurangzeb reintroduces the jizya on non-Muslims, reversing Akbar's policy — a measure that deepens opposition among Rajputs, Marathas and others.

events.title: Aurangzeb's 25-year Deccan war
events.summary: Aurangzeb moves the court to the Deccan. He executes Sambhaji, but the Marathas under Rajaram and Tarabai fight on, and the war drains the empire's treasury and army.

events.title: Bijapur and Golconda conquered
events.summary: The last two Deccan sultanates fall. The empire reaches its greatest extent, from Kabul to Gingee, but holding the Deccan proves impossible.

events.title: Aurangzeb dies
events.summary: Aurangzeb dies near Ahmednagar, aged 88. His sons fight it out; Muazzam wins at Jajau and reigns as Bahadur Shah I.

events.title: The Sayyid brothers make and unmake emperors
events.summary: In seven years four emperors are placed on the throne by court factions, chiefly the Sayyid brothers, who depose and kill Farrukhsiyar in 1719 — with a Maratha army present in Delhi.

events.title: Banda Singh Bahadur executed
events.summary: The Sikh commander who had led a peasant uprising across Punjab is captured and executed in Delhi.

events.title: Successor states emerge
events.summary: Governors become hereditary rulers: Murshid Quli Khan in Bengal (1717), Nizam-ul-Mulk in Hyderabad (1724), and soon Awadh. The emperor's authority shrinks to the area around Delhi.

events.title: The Marathas in the north
events.summary: Bajirao reaches Delhi (1737), Malwa is ceded (1738), and in 1752 the Marathas formally undertake to protect the emperor — until Abdali crushes them at Panipat in 1761.

events.title: Nader Shah at Karnal — Delhi sacked
events.summary: The Persian ruler Nader Shah defeats Muhammad Shah at Karnal, sacks Delhi and carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: Robert Clive's victory in Bengal makes the East India Company a territorial power in the richest Mughal province.

events.title: Battle of Buxar
events.summary: The Company defeats the combined armies of Emperor Shah Alam II, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and Mir Qasim of Bengal.

events.title: Treaty of Allahabad — the Diwani
events.summary: Shah Alam II grants the Company the diwani — the right to collect the revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The Company becomes a ruling power under the cover of Mughal authority.

events.title: The emperor under Maratha protection
events.summary: Maratha armies restore Shah Alam II to Delhi; Mahadji Shinde becomes his regent and the real power in the capital.

events.title: British take Delhi
events.summary: Gerard Lake defeats Shinde's army outside Delhi. The blind Shah Alam II becomes a British pensioner; the emperor's writ now runs no further than the Red Fort.

events.title: Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last emperor
events.summary: Bahadur Shah II, a poet and calligrapher known by his pen name Zafar, succeeds to a throne with no real power.

events.title: Revolt of 1857 — Delhi besieged
events.summary: Rebel soldiers from Meerut reach Delhi and proclaim the 82-year-old Bahadur Shah Zafar emperor of Hindustan. The British besiege and storm Delhi in September; Zafar surrenders at Humayun's Tomb.

events.title: End of the dynasty
events.summary: Zafar is tried and exiled to Rangoon, where he dies in 1862. The British Crown takes over India from the East India Company.
